conventions.convention: The datum has finitely many simple indices, row-coroot convention ⟨α_j,h_i⟩=a_ij, positive integer symmetrizers d_i, q_i=q^{d_i}, and K_i=K_{d_i h_i}. The lattice pairing need not be perfect or separating.

In [E_i,P]=(K_i Q−K_i^{-1}R)/(q_i−q_i^{-1}), e_i'(P)=R and e_i''(P)=Q. Actual negative-half weights are −ν; e_i' raises actual weight by α_i and lowers positive height. Its left-generator twist is q_i^{-a_ij}.

Quantum weight modules carry a chosen P-label grading, and morphisms preserve it. Label spaces are simultaneous toral eigenspaces only when the pairing separates P. Integrability requires local nilpotence of both E_i and F_i, without uniform exponents, finite-dimensionality, or bounded support.

The module polarization uses the linear anti-involution σ fixing q and K_h, with σ(E_i)=q_i F_i K_i^{-1} and σ(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_i E_i. This differs from the semilinear torus-inverting anti-involution τ.

The half form is homogeneous, has B(1,1)=1, and satisfies B(F_i P,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q). Homogeneity, equivalently counit normalization, is essential. Its divided-power rank-one norm is 1/[a]_{q_i²}!, so it is A-valued on the word lattice, not on all of U_A^-.
A=Z[q,q^{-1}] is not a PID. U_A is the generated subalgebra inside U_q, including every shifted toral binomial T_{i,c,t}; its definition asserts no freeness or integral triangular decomposition.

The q=1 comparison is in characteristic zero. At algebra level, all K_h=1 are imposed by the positive quotient; they need not equal 1 in the unquotiented specialization. At operator level, the lattice itself must split into its intersections with label spaces.

AC is assumed by the published generic-half pairing and PBW-rank supplier. Its uses are inherited by separation, half-form nondegeneracy, and local half specialization. Semisimplicity separately assumes AC for selecting a maximal independent family of simple submodules.
The normalized Hecke generators satisfy H_s²=1+(v^{-1}−v)H_s, bar sends v to v^{-1}, and lower KL coefficients lie in vZ[v]. The generic-parameter dictionary is q=v^{-2}.

load_bearing.statement: For a dominant integral label λ, M(λ)/Σ_i U_q F_i^{(⟨λ,h_i⟩+1)}v_λ is nonzero, integrable, has finite-dimensional label spaces and support contained in λ−Q_+, and equals the canonical highest-weight module L(λ), simple also as an ordinary module. Every nonzero integrable cyclic highest-weight module of weight λ is uniquely isomorphic to it after prescribing its highest vector. Its character equals the classical integrable highest-weight character of the explicitly regularized realization.

Every nonzero graded quotient V of the dominant Serre quotient with nonzero highest line has the classical simple integrable highest-weight character. The Serre quotient is simple and universal among integrable cyclic highest-weight modules. The ordinary-word lattice V_R over R=Q[q]_(q−1) is U_A-stable, finite free on each label, and has the classical simple integrable q=1 fibre.

For λ∈P, the highest-weight coefficient formula B(av_λ,bv_λ)=η(σ(a)b) constructs the unique normalized homogeneous contravariant Verma form. Its radical equals the sum of all proper graded submodules, and it descends nondegenerately to L(λ). An integrable cyclic graded quotient with nondegenerate descended form is ordinarily simple. The highest divided-power lattice in L(λ) has A-valued form values.

There is exactly one normalized homogeneous half form with (F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'Q); it is symmetric, orthogonal between different root degrees, and nondegenerate on each finite-dimensional root component. It is A-valued on the word lattice. On divided powers, (F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=δ_ab/[a]_{q_i²}!, and all divided-lattice values lie in the localization inverting the quantum factorials.

e_i' preserves U_A^-. The finite ordinary-derivative sum P_i=Σ_n(−1)^n q_i^{-n(n−1)/2}F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n projects U_q^- onto ker e_i' along F_i U_q^-. Every x∈U_A^- has a unique finite expansion Σ_n F_i^{(n)}x_n, with e_i'x_n=0 and x_n=q_i^{n(n−1)/2}P_i(e_i')^n x∈U_A^-; both string-shift operators preserve U_A^-.

Divided powers multiply with Gaussian coefficients; toral binomials cross E_j and F_j by the stated index shifts; E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=Σ_{t=0}^{min(a,b)}F_i^{(b−t)}T_{i,2t−a−b,t}E_i^{(a−t)}. Cross-half divided powers commute for different indices, and same-half divided powers commute when a_ij=0. U_A is spanned over A by U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+, without an independence assertion.

For one simple torus, {K_i^δ T_{i,0,t}:δ∈{0,1},t≥0} is an A-basis of the generated integral torus. For the full torus, multiplying the products of these node bases by the explicitly chosen representatives of P^∨/Σ_i Z(d_i h_i) gives an A-basis of U_A^0.

Over R=Q[q]_(q−1), the half components are finite free and specialize to the classical halves; the stated toral basis and negative-toral-positive tensor decomposition hold. For every characteristic-zero field k at q=1, the positive toral quotient is k[H_i], with T_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t), and the positive full quotient is U(g_der)_k.

concerns.concern: The Statement covers every λ∈P, but Step 3.1 cites the uniqueness part of def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module, whose Definition introduces λ as dominant. That definition's Step 2.2 proves uniqueness without using dominance, so the argument extends immediately; the consuming proof should explicitly state that extension rather than cite a broader domain than the definition states.

Step 1.1 says 'descend on d=ℓ(w)−ℓ(x)' while starting at p_{w,w}=1 and constructing lower x from already constructed higher y. The actual construction descends in Bruhat order and increases d. The coefficient argument is sound, but the induction direction is misnamed.

alerts.finding: F1 says each V(ν) 'has support ν−Q_+'. The cited existence theorem asserts support contained in that cone. If read as equality, the wording fails already for the rank-one trivial module V(0), whose support is {0}. Step 1.2 needs only containment, so this appears to be a wording correction rather than a defect in the tensor argument.

F5 says 'the Serre ideal vanishes, so π_λ is a field isomorphism carrying U_A^- onto V_A(λ)'. Step 4.1 supplies the intended fixed-degree qualification. Regularization does not remove the negative-half Serre relations, and the full highest-weight projection always has the singular-vector kernel supplied by the batch-5 existence theorem. State explicitly that the highest-weight kernel component vanishes in the selected degree and restrict the displayed isomorphisms to those components.

F1 attributes the divided coproduct formulas ΔF_i^{(r)}=Σ_t q_i^{-t(r−t)}F_i^{(r−t)}K_i^t⊗F_i^{(t)} and ΔE_i^{(r)}=Σ_t q_i^{t(r−t)}E_i^{(t)}⊗K_i^{-t}E_i^{(r−t)} to lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities and def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form. Neither supplier states a coproduct formula, and this consumer's deps omit thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra. The formulas follow by the q-binomial expansion of that theorem's q-commuting summands; supply that short derivation and the actual Hopf dependency.

seams_checked.note: The substantive uses preserve the e_i' orientation, ordinary derivative powers in the projector, chosen label gradings, highest-weight universality, polarization norms and localized half-form denominators. The tensor-map F1 support wording strengthens containment to apparent equality, as routed in alerts. Reverse references on the supplier page do not supply a logical premise from this consumer.

The integral form, integral skew-string coefficients, half-form normalization, toral basis and local q=1 comparison are otherwise preserved. The fixed-degree projection wording and the unsupported attribution of divided coproduct formulas are recorded in alerts. The supplier page leaves global freeness and integral triangular decomposition to later results and does not assume those conclusions.

The KLR comparison distinguishes B_K from B_L=C_νB_K with C_ν=Π_i(1−q_i²)^{-ν_i}, giving divided-power norms Π_{a=1}^n(1−q_i^{2a})^{-1}. It retains the inherited AC use for nondegeneracy. The Serre-map proof first works over Q(q), then restricts using the divided-word generators and the free shift-orbit target; it does not infer an integral presentation from the definition alone. No reverse logical use of KLR categorification was found in the assigned suppliers.
